analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: ASML tool demand; IFX good enough; VOD inline; TSMC Oct inline; BT delays Starlink; Auto1 appoints CFO
key_insights: US equities rebounded sharply on 9 Nov: S&P 500 +2.3%, Nasdaq 100 +3.4%, semis +6.8% even as Nvidia fell 4.3%. More than 420 S&P names rose. The desk attributes the move to short covering and fresh tech buying after last week's sell-off.
Oil fell about 5% to $85 on Iran de-escalation. Trump said extensive strikes are highly unlikely, conditional on Iran signing a very strong agreement.
Asia is higher, with regional equities up 1.8% and Korea up 4%. The desk calls this catch-up with the earlier US and European rebound, not a fresh signal.

Positioning is light. US Info Tech net allocation is 14.4% of US net market value, near multi-year lows (1st, 1st and 3rd percentiles on 1, 3 and 5-year lookbacks). Semis positioning has almost fully round-tripped in 2026. The market is hesitant to give an all-clear before CPI and CoreWeave/Nebius earnings this week.

GIR (Jim Schneider) calls semis clearly oversold. The 35GW of 2027 datacenter capacity is largely already under construction, which leaves near-term AI capex relatively insulated. GIR sees compelling risk/reward in NVDA, AVGO, AMAT, LRCX and memory.

ASML: DigiTimes reports Samsung and SK Hynix are racing to secure EUV tools for DRAM/HBM expansion ahead of expected 2027-28 supply shortfalls. SK Hynix disclosed an order of about KRW12tn, and both companies reportedly target KRW10-20tn. The desk reads this as support for ASML order visibility and pricing power. The desk also notes investor questions on whether a Democratic sweep brings the Match Act back into focus as a headwind for ASML China sales.

Infineon Q4 and guidance were in line. Q4 EBIT of €1.12B beat consensus of €1.10B, with margin 23.8% vs 23.3% consensus. FY27 revenue guide is about €20B vs €19.8bn consensus. Datacenter power supplies are guided to close to €4B, ahead of the sellside but at the bottom end of the buyside's >€4bn hope. The desk calls the FX assumption conservative and expects management to set beatable guidance.
TSMC October sales were NT$586bn (+14.7% MoM, +59.7% YoY), tracking at 34% of 4Q26 consensus, in line. Q4 is seasonally the peak for advanced-node mobile and CPU shipments.

Vodafone was in line. Group service revenue was 1.8% ahead. H1 adjusted EBITDAaL of €6.45B was 0.9% light, with an FCF miss. FY27 guidance was raised to adjusted EBITDAaL €13.2-13.4B and adjusted FCF €2.8-3.0B, which the desk reads as about a 2% FCF upgrade to the Street driven by UK and Europe, mostly cost cuts. Germany is the bear debate: ex the 1&1 wholesale revenue and the ECJ provision, German EBITDA is still down about 4% y/y in H1, and Vodafone Deutschland will cut 2,300 jobs.
Sunrise was in line with the Street and reiterated FY26 guidance. Q3 revenue was CHF732m. Operating FCF beat on lower capex while FCF missed on working capital.

SpaceX plans a gas-fired power plant and supercomputing facility at Starbase in Texas with initial investment of about $24 billion. The desk calls it the cleanest positive in 24h, since it monetizes existing offtake and sidesteps Texas grid politics.

The Senate advanced a bipartisan permitting bill 73-25 on a procedural vote, not final passage, and the House is likely the bigger hurdle. The desk expects more conditions on datacenter development but no nationwide moratorium, which it reads as benefiting infrastructure and well-capitalised developers.

The White House is considering new export controls on Nvidia's advanced AI chips, possibly within this year's NDAA, per The Information. The desk cites this as a reason for NVDA weakness against the rally.

Europe datacenters: GIR's call with the EUDCA Secretary General said European development is unaffected by US midterms, the market could more than double by the early 2030s, and power grids are the single largest bottleneck.

BT is delaying its Starlink broadband launch after service disruptions in Ukraine, per the FT, though the service is ready. The CEO confirmed a launch in the coming months, versus an earlier target of 2H26. Ukraine's access has since been restored.

Memory and tools: Tesla and SpaceX's Terafab reportedly targets 1m wafers per month, including 700k DRAM, close to Samsung's reported capacity. Onsemi reportedly abandoned its US$2 billion SiC expansion in the Czech Republic, with reports linking it to cheaper Chinese wafers.
Away from GS: JPM upgraded SAP to Overweight and Berenberg raised Auto Trader to Buy from Hold. AUTO1 appointed Jörg Pietzner CFO effective 1 January 2027.

earnings_insights: Infineon Q4 (reported 10 Nov, basis not specified by the desk): revenue €4.71B in line, EBIT €1.12B vs consensus est €1.10B, margin 23.8% vs consensus est 23.3% and company guidance of about 23%.

Infineon FY27 guidance (assumed EUR/USD 1.15): revenue about €20B vs Infront consensus est €19.8bn, datacenter power supplies close to €4B (buyside wanted >€4bn), adjusted gross margin mid-to-high 40% range, segment result margin mid 20% range, investments €3.0-3.5B, FCF about €1.8B. Desk says guided topline and segment result are 1% and 3% ahead of Vara consensus est. Humanoid robot content was raised from 500 to 1,000 per robot.

Vodafone H1 (reported 10 Nov): adjusted EBITDAaL €6.45B, 0.9% light vs consensus, with an FCF miss. Group service revenue was 1.8% ahead and Europe 1% ahead. German EBITDA is down about 4% y/y excluding 1&1 wholesale revenue and the ECJ provision.
Vodafone FY27 guidance raised: adjusted EBITDAaL €13.2-13.4B (Street est 13.3bn) and adjusted FCF €2.8-3.0B (Street est 2.8bn).
Sunrise Q3 (reported): revenue CHF732m, adjusted EBITDAaL slightly ahead of consensus at CHF264.8M, adjusted FCF CHF32.5M vs CHF36.7M a year ago. FY26 guidance confirmed.
TSMC October monthly sales (reported 10 Nov) of NT$586bn track at 34% of 4Q26 consensus, in line.
CoreWeave and Nebius report earnings later this week. The market is cautious ahead of both.

risk_factors: US CPI tomorrow and CoreWeave/Nebius earnings this week could stall the rebound.
Possible new US export controls on Nvidia AI chips via the NDAA.
Democratic gains could revive the Match Act, a headwind for ASML China sales.
The Senate permitting bill passed only a procedural vote and faces a harder House vote. It could add conditions on datacenter development.
The Iran de-escalation is conditional on Iran signing an agreement.
German telecom trends and KPIs remain weak.
Memory capacity expansion may face delays and higher equipment costs.
GIR's Kickstart note says volatility may persist, and it prefers cash and long-duration bonds near term.
vol_and_positioning: US Info Tech net allocation is 14.4% of US net market value, in the 1st, 1st and 3rd percentiles on 1-year, 3-year and 5-year lookbacks (GS PB).
Semis positioning has almost fully round-tripped in 2026.
Last week featured large cuts in gross and net exposure, and a big cut in tech length specifically.

On 9 Nov the desk saw a mix of covering and long buying across tech, excluding NVDA. HFs were net buyers, largely in macro products. Asset manager flows were roughly flat, with demand in tech and financials and supply in communication services.
Floor activity was a 5 on a 1-10 scale.
geopolitical: Iran de-escalation: Trump said it is highly unlikely he will order extensive strikes on Iran, conditional on Iran signing a very strong agreement. Crude fell about 5% to $85.
US post-midterm politics: the desk flags that a Democratic sweep could bring the Match Act back into focus, a headwind for ASML and China sales.
White House officials discussed possible new export controls on Nvidia advanced AI chips as part of this year's NDAA, per The Information.
Ukraine's Starlink access was disrupted and later fully restored. The US government denied ordering the restrictions, and BT delayed its Starlink launch.
The UK backed a proposed Shetland-Norway subsea data cable amid concerns about interference with undersea infrastructure.
Onsemi reportedly cancelled a Czech SiC expansion, with reports linking it to competition from cheaper Chinese wafers.
